title: Truth and Lies
summary: We talked about lying and telling the truth, and when a white lie is OK. We read people's opinions about lying for their company and learnt words like consequences, reputation and beneficial. We practised the second conditional with 'if' and 'unless', and the short form 'd for 'would'.

vocab.def: To tell a person something that you know is not true.
vocab.example: If I lied to my boss once, he would never trust me again.

ar.d: أن تقول لشخص شيئاً تعرف أنه غير صحيح

zh.d: 对某人说你明知不真实的话

de.d: jemandem etwas sagen, von dem man weiß, dass es nicht stimmt

fr.d: dire à quelqu'un une chose que l'on sait fausse

vocab.def: To say something untrue on a topic, for example your age.
vocab.example: Would you lie about your past to impress someone you love?

ar.d: أن تقول كلاماً غير صحيح عن موضوع معيّن، مثل عمرك

es.d: persona que conoces un poco, pero no es un amigo cercano

es.d: sin entradas ni productos para comprar

fr.d: il ne reste plus de billets ou d'articles à acheter

grammar.title: Second conditional
grammar.explain: We use the second conditional to talk about imaginary situations in the present or future and their results. The situation is not real now, or it is not likely.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم الجملة الشرطية الثانية للحديث عن مواقف خيالية في الحاضر أو المستقبل ونتائجها. الموقف غير حقيقي الآن أو غير مرجَّح الحدوث.
form: If + past simple, would / wouldn't + infinitive
would / wouldn't + infinitive + if + past simple (no comma)
Put a comma only when the 'if' part comes first
If I / he / she / it were ... ('were' is better than 'was')
Question: Would you + infinitive + if + past simple?
Short form: I would = I'd, you would = you'd, she would = she'd

examples.en: I would lie only if it didn't have any consequences for others.
examples.note: Imaginary situation. The main part comes first, so there is no comma.

examples.en: If I found money on the street, I'd take it to the police.
examples.note: The 'if' part comes first, so we use a comma. I'd = I would.

examples.en: Would you be surprised if I told you everybody lies?
examples.note: Question form. 'Would you' often sounds like /wʊdʒu/.

examples.en: I would change many laws if I were the president.
If I had a million dollars, I would buy a house by the beach.
examples.note: Not real: I don't have a million dollars.

mistakes.wrong: If I would find money, I would keep it.
mistakes.right: If I found money, I would keep it.
mistakes.why: No 'would' in the 'if' part. Use the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: She will only lie if it didn't affect the company.
mistakes.right: She would only lie if it didn't affect the company.
mistakes.why: The second conditional uses 'would', not 'will' (correction from class).

mistakes.wrong: If he take the money, I would call the police.
mistakes.right: If he took the money, I would call the police.
mistakes.why: Use the past simple after 'if' (correction from class).

mistakes.wrong: I would tell her, if she asked me.
mistakes.right: I would tell her if she asked me.
mistakes.why: No comma when the main part comes first.

quiz.q: If I ___ a lot of extra money in my bank account, I would tell the bank.
quiz.why: Use the past simple in the 'if' part.

quiz.q: What ___ you do if your friend's cat ran away?
quiz.why: The main part of the second conditional uses 'would'.

quiz.q: If I ___ you, I would tell her the truth.
quiz.why: We say 'If I were you' in the second conditional.

options: I'd lie, if it didn't hurt anyone.
I'd lie if it didn't hurt anyone.
I'd lie if it doesn't hurt anyone.
quiz.why: No comma when the main part is first, and the 'if' part needs the past simple.

quiz.q: If he ___ your painting, he wouldn't put it on the wall.
'I'd tell the truth.' What does I'd mean here?
quiz.why: Before an infinitive (tell), I'd = I would.

grammar.title: Unless in conditionals
grammar.explain: 'Unless' means 'if ... not' or 'except if'. We use it in the condition part. The verb after 'unless' is positive, because 'unless' already has the 'not' meaning.
grammar.explain_ar: كلمة unless تعني «إلا إذا» أو «إذا لم». نستخدمها في جزء الشرط، ويكون الفعل بعدها مُثبَتاً وليس منفياً لأن معنى النفي موجود فيها أصلاً.
form: unless + past simple = if + not + past simple
would / wouldn't + infinitive + unless + past simple

examples.en: I wouldn't lie unless I were sure it would benefit the company.
examples.note: = I wouldn't lie if I weren't sure it would benefit the company.

examples.en: Unless my survival was in danger, I wouldn't lie for the company.
examples.note: I would lie only in this one case.

examples.en: You wouldn't be able to pass the exam unless you studied.

mistakes.wrong: I wouldn't lie unless I weren't sure.
mistakes.right: I wouldn't lie unless I were sure.
mistakes.why: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so don't add another 'not'.

mistakes.wrong: Unless I would know the answer, I would ask.
mistakes.right: Unless I knew the answer, I would ask.
mistakes.why: No 'would' after 'unless'. Use the past simple.

quiz.q: I wouldn't tell him ___ he asked me directly.
'Unless you hurried, you would miss the bus' means:
options: If you hurried, you would miss the bus.
If you didn't hurry, you would miss the bus.
You hurried and missed the bus.

quiz.q: I wouldn't lie unless I ___ in danger.
quiz.why: After 'unless' the verb is positive and in the past simple.

quiz.q: She wouldn't buy that phone unless it ___ cheaper.
quiz.why: Past simple ('were') after 'unless' in the second conditional.

quiz.q: Which has the same meaning as 'I wouldn't go if they didn't invite me'?
options: I would go unless they invited me.
I wouldn't go unless they didn't invite me.
I wouldn't go unless they invited me.
quiz.why: 'If they didn't invite me' = 'unless they invited me'.

phrases.use: Giving a careful answer, not just yes or no

phrases.en: We don't have similar views on ...
phrases.use: Saying you don't agree (teacher's correction of 'We are not similar')

phrases.en: Would you be surprised if I told you ...?
If I were you, I'd tell the truth.

phrases.en: I was just about to call you.
Sorry I'm late, the traffic was terrible.
I've already left home, give me five minutes.
This is delicious! / You look great!

Reporting what a few people said
Reporting that nobody in the group agreed
